t: It is the sense of Congress that a balance is needed in human space flight between using and building upon existing capabilities and investing in and enabling new capabilities. Technology development provides the potential to develop an increased ability to operate and extend human presence in space, while at the same time enhance the nation’s economic development and aid in addressing challenges here on Earth. Additionally, the establishment of in-space capabilities, use of space resources, and the ability to repair and reuse systems in space can contribute to the overall goals of extending human presence in space in an international manner, consistent with section 301(a).

fable.w: The tempting reading is that extending human presence in space "in an international manner" implies coordination with outside parties. That phrase states a policy aspiration and creates no consultation, comment, hearing, advisory body, or right to sue. The section is a sense-of-Congress statement on balancing existing and new space flight capabilities, with no outside party brought into any federal decision.
fable.s: It is the sense of Congress that a balance is needed in human space flight between using and building upon existing capabilities and investing in and enabling new capabilities.

opus.w: This is a sense-of-Congress statement about balancing existing and new human space flight capabilities. It creates no requirement or option for the federal government to consult or coordinate with outside parties before deciding anything. The phrase "in an international manner" describes a broad goal, not a process that brings outsiders into a federal decision, so it does not count as participation.
opus.s: It is the sense of Congress that a balance is needed in human space flight between using and building upon existing capabilities and investing in and enabling new capabilities.

That reading doesn't hold up. This is a non-binding sense-of-Congress statement about policy priorities. It names no outside party and sets up no process like consultation, comment, a hearing, an advisory body or a right to sue before a federal decision.
